settings.text: A jewellery house built on what a flower means, and on the discipline of leaving things out.

settings.title: Meaning
settings.text: Every form starts with a flower that already means something to someone.

settings.title: Line
settings.text: Reduced until only the gesture remains — the restraint of Italian design.

settings.title: Hand
settings.text: Shaped, set and finished by hand, in numbers small enough to care about.

settings.statement: In India, a flower is never only a flower. It is a greeting, a blessing, a thing you give when words are not enough.
settings.text:
Florève begins with that idea. In marigold at a doorway, jasmine in the hair, petals offered with both hands — the flower carries feeling, and it has done so for as long as anyone can remember.

We take that meaning and give it an Italian discipline of line: reduced, balanced, nothing ornamental for its own sake. What remains is shaped by hand, slowly.
Because it is how we welcome, bless, celebrate and remember — and it lasts a day.

A flower is given at a birth, a wedding, a homecoming and a farewell. It is placed at a threshold, tucked into hair, laid at the feet of something loved. No other object carries so much feeling and asks so little.

Its only failing is that it fades. So we studied the part that matters — the turn of a petal at its edge, the way a bud holds itself before it opens — and gave it a form that stays.

settings.image_alt: A single flower studied before it is drawn

settings.text: An Indian heart, an Italian line

From India we take the reverence — that adornment is not vanity but expression, and that a flower given by hand carries intention.

From the Italian tradition we take the discipline of form: proportion held exactly, ornament earned rather than added, the confidence to stop. Neither is decoration for the other. A piece needs both to feel finished.

settings.image_alt: Work in progress at the bench

settings.title: The study
settings.text: We begin with a real flower — how it is held, given and worn — before a single line is drawn.

settings.title: The hand
settings.text: Each piece is shaped, soldered and set by hand. Nothing is stamped out, nothing is hurried.

settings.title: The finish
settings.text: Surfaces are polished by hand until light moves across them the way it moves across a petal.

settings.heading: How a feeling becomes an object

settings.quote: A flower is how we say the thing we cannot. We only made the sentence last longer.
